Get the noscript or ghostery addon for your web browser. This blocks javascript from running on web pages. It's not giving you complete safety, but it eliminates one avenue of tracking/attacks. Sometimes the content is hosted on an external server, which i run across in web streams. In that scenario, all you can really do is start allowing blocked sites temporarily until you have allowed the sites needed to display the content.

Here's the deal: almost literally everything bad that could possibly happen to you just from visiting a website starts with "scripts". In this context a script is a piece of javascript code on a webpage. When you visit the page the scripts execute code on your pc. If it is malicious and you are vulnerable you get fucked: IP address / DNS server revealed, malware etc. Using a tool like noscript allows you to selectively block scripts.
